But his lawless conduct was rebuked many times by those holy first desert-dwellers of Klarjeti,
by the fathers and by the whole flock of the catholic church, and above all by Father Gregory, because he was the archimandrite of those glorious desert monasteries.
But Tsqiri, overcome by pride, threw off the fear of God completely. He secretly summoned a layman of Ancha,
a worthless [?] and poor man who was a very strong archer. He promised to give him three griv of wheat and five goats,
and sent him to Khandzta to kill Father Gregory. On the way the man learned from someone that Gregory was at the Khandzta farm and would be coming home that day.
So he went into the Khandzta forest to lie in wait, holding a drawn bow in his hands.

Now the blessed Father Gregory was coming down alone from his own farm to Khandzta. As he walked along the road he was reciting from memory the readings composed by the holy Father Ephrem, lamenting and weeping.
Yet he rejoiced in spirit, because by the grace of the Holy Spirit he was seeing divine visions.
Then that wretched man saw a great sign from above over the saint: a very bright pillar of light, reaching up to heaven, was covering him.
Above his head was a cross too bright for the eyes to look at, and it encircled him like a rainbow appearing beautifully in rainy weather.
When the man saw this glory over him, great trembling seized him. The sinews of his arms went slack, and he lay collapsed on the ground from that great terror.
The blessed Gregory said to him: "O wretched man, carry out the command of the one who sent you!
You are a denier of Christianity, since you are shedding the blood of an innocent old man for a worthless payment.
"Or have you not come to kill me over three grivi of millet and five goats, O foolish man?" Then the man begged him with tears:
"Have mercy, holy one of God, on this wretch who would have murdered you, and be like Christ, who forgives his murderers when they repent,
for no strength is left in me because of the terrible vision of you, which struck me down."
Then the saint mercifully made the sign of the cross over him and healed him, because many blows had struck him. And he sent him home rejoicing.
The man told Tsqiri everything that had happened. But Tsqiri raged all the more and added blindness on top of blindness.
He did many evil things to Father Gregory, to the holy fathers of that time, and to other faithful laypeople as well.
Those who had always rightly rebuked him joined together and reported everything to the great ruler Ashot the kouropalates.
At his command, all the clergy of the catholic church of Ancha wrote a letter to the catholicos of Kartli,
and through him worthy bishops were brought to Ancha. All the desert fathers gathered there with them.
And the blessed mother Febronia, the worker of miracles, came to that holy council, which resembled those first holy ones, and with them came all the priests and the clergy of Ancha.
And before the bishops they set out the case of Tskiri and his lawlessness. Those trustworthy, miracle-working men laid out the grounds of his shameful deeds to his face.
Then those faithful chief priests deposed him from his rank.
And Father Gregory and Mother Febronia brought him down, still dressed in his altar vestments, and stripped him before the altar,
and all of them together cast him out of the catholic church like a rotten limb. Like the heretics, he was driven out as one who had broken the law in every respect.
But because God's help had left him, he had no means left at all, and he went to Tbilisi to the emir Sahak, his own lord.
And through his complaint the curopalates was drawn in, as it were [?], and once again Tskiri took the see of Ancha by force, so that he could take revenge on Father Gregory.
Then he gathered the people of Ancha and sent them to destroy Khandzta. They arrived just at sunrise, and Father Gregory said to them:
"Children, give me and my brothers time until midday, so that we may pray before Christ in the holy church,
and call on Saint George and all the saints for help, and the Lord will work a good miracle."
And they listened to the old man's word, because they had seen miracles done by him.
And at the time of their tearful supplication the Lord heard their petition and made it known to them through a holy angel:
"Divine vengeance has overtaken that wicked enemy of yours. Look, a messenger will come saying that he has died. Even though he will be alive for two more days, this is so
that he will not be worthy to be buried in the episcopal see, and so that everyone will believe in his deposition. But his heart is already dead."
And when the fathers, who were equal to the angels, heard this joyful news from the angel, they rejoiced greatly and gave glory to God, who alone works wonders.
And they understood the scripture that says: "Wrath kills the foolish." This applied to the man who always practised disorder yet counted himself among the righteous.
Then the blessed Gregory came out of the church joyful and said to them:
"Fear no longer the tyranny of the one who sent you, for the Lord has struck him dead in his wrath."
And at that very moment a man arrived who said to those men: "Do not dare to destroy glorious Khandzta any longer, for the one who wanted to destroy it has died."
Then those men rejoiced. The fathers gave them hospitality, and they went joyfully to their homes, glorifying God.
But let us return to the earlier account. When Tskiri sent the people to Khandzta, he himself went to Kortha, because his stored-up goods were there, and he meant to carry them off.
And on the way, after they had eaten bread, he fell asleep and saw a terrible vision. It convicted him of his evil deeds, and above all of the evil he had done to the people of Khandzta.
Now a godly priest from Ancha was with him, and the Lord revealed to this priest the evil death of Tskiri.
And that priest sent his own disciple to Khandzta and told them for certain of Tskiri's death.
And as soon as Tskiri reached Kortha, he died, and they buried him there until the second coming of the Lord.
And when the trial of that time had passed away, the holy see of the icon of Christ the living God spread the joy of peace over its flocks, as good shepherds shone forth.
But in these last times of ours the poor rejoice by the grace of the Lord, by the intercession of the saints of old, and by the bodily labours of our glorious kings,
who were truly devout servants of God, builders of holy churches and destroyers of the camp of the barbarians,
the pride of true Christians and the joy of monks. Among them was found the son of the great Adarnase the curopalates, Bagrat, eristav of eristavs (duke of dukes),
by the power of God a great sovereign, in the days of Ezra, the venerable chief father and bishop of Ancha, son of the glorious nobles the Dapanchulis.
This Bagrat was praised for his understanding. He was a builder of holy churches, a seeker and collector of divine books, and one who worthily glorified all the saints.
May the intercession of the saints always help him, here and forever. He renewed this Life of the blessed father Gregory by adding the miracles that had been left out.
May he be counted by Christ the King among the number of those first holy kings, through the prayer of the venerable Gregory and of all the saints.
This glorious king removed the reproach from us, the poor children of father Gregory, and brought shame on the one who reproached us in ignorance.

May the Lord wipe away completely the reproach of the sins he bears, through the entreaty of the venerable fathers, and with them through the grace of the blessed father Gregory, who lived on earth like an angel.
And in the time of his old age he gave this command to the brotherhoods of Khandzta:
"In this monastery let no one build a chapel next to the cells for celebrating the liturgy, for it is improper, unless it is the will of the community,
apart from that great common church, for this reason: when the dean rings the bell for the hour of the liturgy, not all the priests will go there,
but they will stay in their own chapels to celebrate the liturgy, and, just like the great church, they will trouble people by asking for offerings,
and the dean will always have to plead with the officiating priests to go to the great church.
And now this rule must be upheld by whoever is obedient to the words of me, the poor Gregory."
This blessed man of God, father Gregory, dwelling-place of the will of Christ and glorious worker of miracles, lived to an extremely old age, for he reached a hundred and two years.
The colour of his face did not change, and his sight did not grow dim. He was strong in body, and no weakness of any kind was found in him until his death,
for he was strengthened by the power of Christ. His pride was the lamp of virginity, the oil of mercy, and love for God and for the brethren.
He greatly loved toil, not only the toil of prayer and fasting. Day and night he also worked with his own hands, as Paul says:
"Whoever does not work, let him not eat." And he was a cheerful host and one who laboured for the poor.
On most days he stayed at Shatberdi, for he had appointed superiors in his own monasteries, and they laboured for them,
And whatever matter was too difficult for them, they would make it known to him, in keeping with the God-given wisdom that dwelt in him always,
until his end, when the wise one went to join the wise in eternal life and reign.
In the days of his old age, while he was at Shatberdi, the brothers who lived at Khandzta became anxious,
for they had heard that the end of this life awaited their spiritual father at Shatberdi.
Then all who had the strength to travel went together to Shatberdi to seek out the holy man.
The brothers of Shatberdi rejoiced at the arrival of their own brothers. But when they understood the reason for their coming, their joy turned to sorrow.
They prayed with prostrations in the holy church of the holy Mother of God. Then the children whom he had begotten spiritually and gathered by his labor bowed down before their blessed father,
and he kissed them all eagerly and longingly and greeted them tenderly, like a sweet father and a kind teacher.
Then the brothers of Khandzta and of Shatberdi greeted one another with a kiss and sat down.
Then the blessed Gregory began to speak to the Khandzta brothers and said to them:
"Brothers and beloved children, tell me, what is the reason that all of you have taken the trouble to come here?" And Epiphanius and Zeno said to the other brothers:

"You should give a worthy answer, so that, as wise disciples speaking to a wise teacher, you may offer the gift of your zeal in worthy words, and so that, through the grace of God, we may hopefully obtain what our souls desire."
Then all of them cried out with one voice: "O holy one of God, father who begot your children spiritually, guardian of our life,
and intercessor for those who believe in Christ: although our brothers of Shatberdi are all pleasing to the Lord and obey your will, which agrees with the will of God,
yet your failure to come to us at Khandzta for so many days is a great shame to us and a reproach against all of us from everyone, for Khandzta is the first fruit of your holy labors.

And now this is why we have come here: so that you will be pleased to go to Khandzta, so that those who cannot come here may be comforted, and so that you may show the other desert monasteries as well your perfect love for us.
And know this: if we do not find a hearing, we will all be found here before you, for at this time it is grievous to us to go to Khandzta without you."
Then the holy man said: "Blessed is Christ, God of all, who has firmly planted his own holy commandment of love in your hearts toward me, your poor old man,
my beloved children, and still more, children of Christ and fulfillers of his holy will. By his own command he called it the gospel,
for by his coming he announced peace to people who were his enemies. Out of love for them he took death upon himself, and he taught all of us
that 'divine love is the head of all the virtues.' And now love has brought you here.
But for me it is hard on both sides: first, because of your distress, and second, because of being separated from these brothers."
Then he summoned all the brothers of Shatberdi and said to them:
"Come, children, join the inhabitants of Khandzta, your brothers, and bring your wills into harmony with one another, for strife flees from the wise. Settle on what is best, in unity.
"But I think that the place built first is owed greater honour by its builder, just as an old man is owed respectful service by a young one."

The brothers of Shatberdi said to him: "Your ruling is true, holy father. If justice had not given it to you, then, as the Lord and your holy prayer live, we would not have [?] yielded to our brothers."
When they had said this and other similar things, as was fitting, the blessed father Gregory said to them all: "Children, the command of Christ has gathered us together today

so that we may now make the firmness of unity and love a law forever for the brothers who will live in these two monasteries in times to come. This is according to the word of the Lord, which he spoke to the apostles:
'By this all will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.' And again he commanded them: 'What I say to you, I say to all.'
Now you also must keep the commandments of the Lord. Honour and love one another, with every virtue and with humility that is without guile, and pray for one another in your holy churches.
And may I, the wretched one, always be remembered in your holy prayers. May you be seen as good in your brotherhood by those near and far.
If any of the brothers wish to move, those of Khandzta to Shatberdi or those of Shatberdi to Khandzta, let no one have the power to refuse to receive them,
or to cause trouble and overturn their intention, or to stop them by force without some just cause.
"But if anyone should unjustly hinder this, he will give account to God on the Day of Judgment, for it is not my will, who am your spiritual father, according to the word of the Apostle:
'Though you have ten thousand tutors, yet you do not have many fathers.'"
As for every other divine rule for the life of the soul, I set it down for you from the beginning. Hold firmly to it forever.
And may the peace of Christ, which surpasses all understanding, keep you all in unity from every harm of soul and body and bring you to the saints."
Then he went into the holy church and, with tears, commended himself to him [?].
After he had given the peace in silence, he gave the kiss to the monks as he came out, and so he set out toward Khandzta.
All the people followed him in tears. The saint stood on a high place among the people of God, offered glory to Christ, and said:
"My Lord Jesus Christ, God, before your coming to earth you were in the world. Now, though you are above the heavens, you are with us to help us through the light of the power of your divinity!
You, Lord, in your mercy led me to these lands with three companions, good and holy priests.
Until their deaths they always offered you holy, bloodless sacrifices without ceasing, and you made them a safe harbour for many souls.
After their deaths you made them worthy to serve at the altar of heaven without tiring, with the holy angels.
And now, Christ, through me you have multiplied those who do your will. For the talent of wisdom that you gave me from my youth, I have multiplied as a faithful servant among your faithful.
"And now the disciples of the kingdom stand before you. Bless them, Christ, as you blessed the holy apostles, and protect my children who are to come in later times,
until the end of the world, according to your will; and have mercy on all your Christians who confess you rightly, O Lord!"
And then he made the sign of the cross over Shatberdi and said:
"Flourish well, Shatberdi, be adorned with grace, and be strengthened by the flame of God, so that from time to time you may offer to the Lord the spotless fruit of your sacrifices,
For behold, I now leave you in peace, and you will no longer see my face in the flesh until the coming of the Lord in glory.
Now, although I part from you in body, in spirit I am always with you to help you."
Then the inhabitants of Shatberdi wept bitter tears at those words, because they would no longer see their teacher in the flesh.
But the holy man said to them: "Children, overcome the pain of your hearts by the wisdom of the spirit, and do not let your minds be shaken, for I promise you this:
Christ will not let you lack anything, here or in the age to come, if you hold fast to what you have learned from me: the rule of monastic life handed down by the early holy fathers.
"And likewise I command my children, generation after generation, to keep this holy teaching.
And if the times, through hardship, should change the rule in a way that does no great harm to the soul, let it be pardoned for that time, but not forever,
and not out of a pursuit of great luxury, about which it is said: 'Nothing angers God so much as excessive luxury.'"
"As for me, when I am made worthy to go to the Lord, I will intercede for you, for you have given me great comfort.
For now, while I am in the body, I pray for myself and for you; but when I am set free from this passing world, I trust in Christ
that my intercession before him will never cease for you, for all who pray to me in faith, and for my children,
so that they may find mercy and help from God, and complete joy forever."
And when he had finished these words, he kissed the brothers of Shatberdi, who were full of tears,
and with much entreaty he persuaded them to return to their own place, and he himself went with the brothers of Khandzta.
Both those who took him away and those who returned received an equal reward from God, for they all had equal faith in and love for their father and teacher.
When the blessed Gregory came from Shatberdi to Khandzta, the hermitages near Khandzta rejoiced, and brothers came from every direction to see the saint,
and they received his blessing and prayer, and went back to their own places full of joy.
For the glory of Khandzta was raised up with an everlasting and visible adornment, since it had been made ready as the resting place forever for those relics worn out by labours.

At that time the blessed father Gregory rejoiced, for he found his monastery in good order, and with great grace he blessed its superior, the faithful father Epiphanius, and all the brothers under his obedience.
Then a certain priest who lived in seclusion begged the blessed man to let him build a small chapel (egut'eri) in his cell for celebrating the liturgy. But the saint said:
"In a community of brothers that is improper. If you build a chapel, all the brothers will build them.

Then, when the dean rings the bell for the liturgy at its hour, a priest will hardly be found in the great church. And much else in it would harm the soul rather than benefit it, and I will not give my approval to it."
After this he said to the great Zenon: "Brother, let us go down to the vineyard which is by the road to Opiza,"
for it was the time of the grape harvest. And the two of them went down together to that vineyard which he had planted, which bore fruit well.
And at that time the blessed father Makari of Opiza came to see his teacher, father Grigol.
And they rejoiced greatly and greeted one another affectionately. Since it was mealtime, they sat down only to eat.
And after the meal they decided to stay there until the next day. And Father Makari, in the course of conversation, asked the blessed Gregory thus:
"If a child of heretics converts to the Orthodox faith, does he need baptism or not?" The holy man said to him:
"The apostle calls them false brethren, those who bear the name of their perverse teachers.
And Paul did not accept that true believers should name themselves after the holy apostles. Instead he rebukes them and says:
'Why are there divisions among you? For each one of you says, "I am of Paul,"' and what follows.
But he called all the orthodox 'Christians.' And now, although Scripture also shows that some heretics are to be baptized and some are not,
"I say this, as you all know: a heretical priest cannot baptize the child of true Christians, even if it is dying unbaptized, for baptism [lit. 'light'] is not with them.
And death unbaptized is better than lawlessness through transgressing the law.
Likewise it is required and right to baptize the children of all heretics, even though each of their heresies appears distinct.
For they are bound to one another by deceptions, like those foxes whose tails Samson tied tail to tail and fastened torches to all their tails.
For they were a figure of all heretics, whose final dwelling is the eternal fire.
For they have become estranged from our holy mother, the one catholic and apostolic Church.
They go astray from the womb, so for them a second birth must be considered.
And they speak lies, for they always preach slander and bear false witness, those who have been anathematized by our holy fathers and teachers.
"And if the children of heretics again seek an assembly, it is no longer proper for them. Rather, there should be caution, and no word at all should be put forward with them for an assembly.
For a believer who does not have the power to work a miracle
should not enter into debate with unbelievers. And since all heretics are called by one name, 'heretic,' their error has also been established as one by the enemy.
For this reason it is required to baptize them all, so that the doubt of contention may be removed and the full joy of the true flocks of Christ may be one."
The blessed Grigol said many words of this kind. And father Makari said to him:
"Truly your ruling is just, holy father. But teach me clearly a word about the Holy Trinity that is fitting to give to those who dispute."
And he said to him: "Learn it from Isaiah, for he learned the equal honour of the Holy Trinity from the seraphim, who cry out unceasingly:
'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Sabaoth.' And Gregory the Theologian says about the three Persons of the Trinity:
'When there are three candles in a house, their light cannot be divided, nor again can they be mixed together.' This is the faith of the Holy Trinity.
And in the 'Treasury' everything is written with all truth, and it says this: 'For the Father is not older than the Son, not even by the blink of an eye.'
Now, as we have learned wisdom from the holy books, it is enough to be your teacher in every respect."
Then the blessed Makar said to him: "Holy father, just as the Lord first gave me the habit of monasticism by your hand,
so now may he also grant me spiritual teaching from your mouth, as a wall of defence for me forever."
And when evening came, all three of those men of God were in one house, and they recited the psalms according to the rule.
But Makar was weary and fell asleep on the bed.
Then that blessed father Gregory and Zenon chanted psalms in a low voice.
And divine grace made them shine with glory, and that dark house was lit up as if by the brightness of the sun.
And when Father Makari awoke, he said: "How wondrously these saints appear!" Father Gregory said to him:
"Brother Makari, why do you marvel at this vision? Have you not heard the scripture: 'God is wonderful among his saints'?"
And so all three of them, glorifiers of the Holy Trinity, rejoiced, and they recited the hymns of matins.
And when dawn broke on those dwellings of peace, they bid one another farewell in peace, and father Makar went away to Opiza, while father Gregory and Zenon went up to their own monastery.
For this Zenon had attained the virtues of his teacher, which is why, after the death of the blessed Gregory, people used to say:
"Zenon is the firm wall of the glorious desert monasteries of Klarjeti."
Now our blessed father Gregory's heart told him of his departure from the flesh and his going to God.
And the Lord made known to him the fulfilment of his wish, as David said: 'The Lord will do the will of those who fear him; he will hear their prayers and save them.'
Then he ordered his brothers to make large wax candles to be offered around all the nearby desert monasteries,
which are Opiza and its branches, Berta and its neighbouring houses, Midznadzori and Tskarostavi, together with their fellow dwellers.
As for Shatberdi, although it is a little farther away than those other desert monasteries,
yet it is their inseparable fellow-brother through the goodness of that people of God and in every rule of divine teaching and the canon of the monastic law.
And in every good work it is honoured equally by God and by men, for it is the pride of all the neighbouring monasteries.
He sent wax candles to all those desert monasteries and sent them word of the day on which they should light them and pray for him.
And they understood that this was the time of his departure from this world, for just as at the death of the holy Mother of God the company of the holy apostles arrived from the ends of the earth,
In the same way the holy fathers gathered at that time, on his appointed day, to honour that blessed old man and to be blessed by him.
He was filled with joy at the sight of them. He blessed them all with the blessing of Christ and said to them:
"May the Lord give you the reward for your labour, the Lord who said:
'I was sick and in prison, and you came to me.' For behold, I am now going out of the prison of the flesh and am being freed from weakness by the grace of God,

who trampled down death by the cross. Just as he did for the thief, he has given his holy cross to all believers as a guide. Just as he did for the holy angels, he has given them that royal seal as the sign of Christianity,
which the souls of believing people have as a protection and for salvation for ever."
Then all the fathers said to the blessed Gregory: "Holy one of God, you who have inherited the works of blessedness according to the commandments of Christ:
you who are poor by your own choice, in the spirit of humility, so as to inherit the kingdom; you who mourn in heart so as to be comforted for ever;
you who are meek in mind and await the good things of paradise; you who hunger and thirst for righteousness,
and have been made worthy of that sweet food of the land that never fails; you who are merciful to the poor: the mercy of God is never parted from you.
"You are pure in your heart and soul and will fully see God. You are a peacemaker among the brothers, and you have reached the peace of the holy angels by being called a son of God.

You took on persecutions and afflictions for God's sake so that you might dwell with Christ. You are a safe harbour for those who are reviled for Christ, and you care for our life with a view to that eternal life.
Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven. For like the righteous apostle Paul,
you have fought the good fight, finished the race and kept the faith, made perfect by good works.
From now on the crown of righteousness awaits you, which the King will grant you in return for your holy labours.
"But do not forget us, your spiritual children, when you come before the face of the good, merciful and compassionate, sweet Lord;
remember your flocks, and do not cease to labor for us before Christ, for you are fully able to help all
who put their hope in your prayers and take refuge in your intercession." And the holy man said to them:
"Although I have prepared myself for the Lord and from my youth have burned [?] like a flame, yet the honor of your words is greater,
fathers who serve Christ. But God seeks zeal from people, and in return he grants the kingdom to those who obey him.
Through the prayers of all of you, may he grant me too to dwell with those who do his will.
Remember my strictness and patience in the monastic life, which you have seen ever since I came to live among you until now,
for this is how the kingdom of heaven must be sought. And pray for me, so that I may be given grace before God by the Lord to help you, my helpers."
Then he said to the brothers who were in Khandzta:
"Children, the commandment that you heard from me before, keep it for the salvation of your souls, and always keep my commemoration."
"And as for me, if I find boldness before Christ, the abundance of his good things shall not be lacking to you in either world.
But this I now command you by the cross of Christ: bury my body with my brothers, for I am not better than they in the acquiring of virtues.
Therefore I beseech you all: never forget me in your prayer to God, me who have always prayed for you and who now offer supplication for you to Christ forever.
"Remember me always in prayer and in the liturgy, me who am made a stranger to you by death, when you see the place of my dwelling in this exile [?],
for behold, until the time of the calling again, my body will return to earth, but may the Lord receive my soul."
And as blessed Gregory was speaking these words, his appearance was then beautifully and radiantly adorned by Christ with unapproachable light.
For a host of the Lord's angels surrounded him, and the fragrance of precious incense filled all the people, the assembly of the fathers.
And that righteous soul had a vision in which he saw the holy heavenly principalities, and from them he now heard this voice of joy:
"Do not be afraid to come with us, servant of Christ, blessed one, for Christ the King of heaven deems you an earthly angel and a heavenly man.
Come now with joy and rejoice with your Lord without end, for you are blessed among men, made ready to inherit that blessed glory, and joyful forever."
These words were heard by some of his disciples, but all of them saw that glorious vision.

Then the blessed man rejoiced fully with that irresistible joy. He made the sign of the cross over his monastery and blessed his brothers, together with all who believe in Christ, with an eternal blessing, and said:
"O Christ the King, since you yourself suffered and were tested, you are able to help those also who are tested by the snares and temptations of the enemy,
for you, O Lord, are the helper of Christians. Protect with your right hand those who trust in your holy name, deliver them from evil, and give them joy that does not grow old.
And save me, your servant, in your kingdom, and remember me with mercy in your reign."
And thus he committed his soul to the Lord and was joined to the company of the angels,
for the bodiless angels and the souls of men are of one nature, and the soul of man has angelic speech, although concerning the ceasing of bodily tongues David says:
"On that day all their thoughts perish"; yet the same one says concerning the souls of the saints that:
"The saints shall boast in glory, they shall rejoice at their commemoration." And they intercede with Christ for those who glorify them.

For until the judgment of the living and the dead they labor on behalf of the believing people in the flesh who beseech them, and they await that perfect joy and gladness according to the promise of their King,
when, at the coming of the Lord in glory, they will pass from glory into a more glorious glory and dwell in it.
And the gathering of the elect from the four winds of heaven, from one end of heaven to the other end of heaven, means this: that by the wind, as by a chariot,
Christ will gather his saints before him for joy and delight forever, when each of them shows his labor to the Lord and receives inexhaustible riches in return.
Then, blessed father, that new martyr of Christ, the blessed John, who went from Khandzta to Jerusalem and was killed for Christ in Baghdad at the hands of the Saracens,
and who shines with miracles, will rejoice together with your chosen children when you present them to Christ.
At that time, what consolation will there be for us, the negligent ones, who are called your disciples,
for love for one another has dried up, every good work has diminished, and deficiency has flourished!?
But after the mercies of God and the intercession of all the saints, our hope rests on your prayers, holy father!
Accept our faith, worthy one, for you know our love. Although we do not see you in the flesh, do not forget us,
but may your grace be a help to us who dwell in your holy deserts, and to all the people, so that we may be found with you in the life of that unending joy.
Now, beloved believers in Christ, it befits all of us to be zealous to do good, each according to our strength, with the mercy of God and the intercession of the saints,
so that we may become worthy of the forgiveness of sins and of great mercy forever.
The death of our blessed father Gregory took place in the hundred and second year of his life, in the year eighty-one of the chronicon.
This Life of his was written ninety years after his death, in the six thousand five hundred and fifty-fourth year of the years elapsed since the beginning [of the world],
when Agathon was patriarch in Jerusalem, Michael was catholicos in Mtskheta, and Ashot the kuropalates was ruler over the Georgians,
son of Adarnase, king of the Georgians; when George, son of King Constantine, was king over the Abkhazians; when Sumbat was eristavi of eristavis,
son of King Adarnase; when Adarnase, son of Bagrat the magistros, was magistros; and when Sumbat, son of David the mampali, was eristavi.
May Christ grant unfading glory to them all!
At that same time Makarios was bishop in Ancha, and the abbots of the monasteries built by the blessed father Gregory were sons of great nobles by lineage:
at Khandzta, Father Theodore, the son of Mtskhveda's sister; and at Shatberdi, Father Gregory, son of Liparit, who was adorned with the name of the great father Gregory.
May Christ fully adorn them with his grace and justify them before him forever!
Through the superior of Khandzta, his brother John, and the writer of this book, Giorgi Merchule,
all three of them together, with zeal, [?] (1228) this Life of the blessed Gregory was written in Khandzta.
May Christ write them in the book of the living, and may he fully show mercy to all believers, so that they may understand the divine gift of earthly things together with heavenly ones.
For in church one reader of a book is equally sufficient for few listeners and for many,

and likewise, whether one person or many receive a blessing, the one who blesses is sufficient; for the good things of Christ toward us never run short, nor does the grace of the saints' intercession.
Therefore may the memory of the blessed Father Gregory today be for us always a hope and a refuge for soul and body, and for all
among the righteous, in the rank of the monks of the leader, our father the great Anthony, in the light that knows no night, as Solomon said:
"Light is upon the righteous always." And again he says:
"But the souls of the righteous are alive in the hand of God," and illumined by that Sun of Righteousness, whom the heavens cannot contain and who was contained in the virgin's womb
ineffably, and who shone forth for our salvation, that light without beginning, Christ our God, for nothing is impossible before him,
It was he who gave his creation, this disk of the sun, such brightness that it spreads over everything visible and lights it up with its light.
And the same almighty God gave the grace of authority to all his saints, and they intercede for us with him unceasingly.
For this reason their memory is celebrated with praise. They always protect those who adorn their feast, they enlighten their souls, and they grant grace to all the faithful,
since each one of them has the power to help those who pray to them with faith. They are always our intercessors before the Holy Trinity,
the Creator of all, to whom belong might, glory, great majesty, and a reign without beginning and without end.
To him are due honor and worship with praise to the ages of ages and the ages to come. Amen.

We heard from our elders about this miracle, which happened long ago. In the time of the disciple of father Gregory, when Epiphanius was abbot of Khandzta, there was a certain rich man in Anchkora named Tserta.
The place now called Tserta's was where he kept his goats. He had a daughter who had been deaf and mute from birth but was otherwise sound in body.
When the girl was thirteen years old, the venerable Epiphanius appeared to her mother in a vision while she slept and said to her:
"Tomorrow, send a man to Khandzta to my liturgy, and from my hands,

the hands of Epiphanius, I will give you the water I have washed them in. Give it to your daughter to drink and anoint her head with it, and Christ will heal her of her afflictions by the grace of all the saints."
The faithful woman did not tell her husband about the vision, because at that time he was hostile toward the monks.
So she sent a man in secret. Blessed Epiphanius knew from the Lord what was going to happen, and he gave the man the water he had washed his hands in.
When it reached the woman, she, with firm faith, anointed her daughter with this blessing (eulogia) from the bloodless sacrifice of the priest who offered it worthily.
The girl then slept for three days and three nights, and when she woke up she said:
"Glory to God, glory to the Holy Trinity, who through the prayer of the blessed father Epiphanius has healed me and delivered me from the devil!"
When her father Tserta saw this miracle, he was amazed and full of joy, and he set off for Khandzta.
When he came within sight of the monastery in the wilderness, he wept aloud over his earlier hostility [?].
Then father Epiphanius greeted him with joy and comforting words and honored him greatly, as far as he was able.
Tserta brought a great offering and presented it before the holy great-martyr George. He gave thanks to Christ the wonder-worker and to his servant Epiphanius,
through whose prayer complete joy spread among them. His daughter lived a good life in this passing world and was saved for eternity.
And may the Lord show full mercy to us as well, through the intercession of all his saints.
Gabriel the teacher, a dweller at Khandzta, a blessed and holy father who lived a life of great ascetic struggle, told us this about Father Basil: during the many years he was abbot of Khandzta,
this was his rule: when he was at home, he would take no nourishment apart from the common table, neither food nor drink.
And at the time of his illness, from which he died while he was abbot, he said to me:
"Son Gabriel, bring me hot korkoti [boiled wheat] from the steward's storehouse."
It had not been prepared that day, so I prepared something else and brought it to him, because he had not tasted anything for many days.
When he learned that this food had not been made for the community that day, he flung away in agitation what he had taken and said to me angrily:
"Why have you sinned, wretched one, and led me astray as well?" In fear I asked his forgiveness and asked him why he was so angry.
He said to me: "Son, in my youth I attended the cell of Father Gregory, and I troubled my father with concerns about my bodily needs.
That man of God had the grace of prophecy from Christ, and he commanded me thus:
'Basil, you will soon be appointed abbot of Khandzta. As for what you are concerned about now, later you will have whatever clothing and bedding you want!'
But I, the old man, your spiritual father, command you now and seal you with the sign of the cross of Christ:

when this word of mine comes to pass in deed, then while you are in Khandzta, be content with the common table for every bodily need; and while you are elsewhere, that honour will be enough to comfort your body.'
"And now, through the many years of my abbacy, I have kept my father's rule in deed.
But you, at the time of my death, were casting me into the punishment due for disobedience. That is why I grew angry with you."
I fell down before him again and marvelled at his great endurance. Then Father Basil blessed me with every blessing and said to me:
"May you be blessed by the Lord, you and all the orthodox people, through the intercession of the holy Mother of God, Saint George and all the saints. Amen."
